sanskrit_verse: आक्रुष्टस्तु समाक्रोशंस्ताडितः प्रतिताडयन्‌ । हत्वापराधिनं चैव नापराधी भवेन्नरः ॥
transliteration: ākruṣṭas tu samākrośaṃs tāḍitaḥ pratitāḍayan / hatvāparādhinaṃ caiva nāparādhī bhaven naraḥ //
sph_interpretive_translation: One who is abused while responding in kind, struck while striking back, or who ends the transgression by eliminating the transgressor—such a person incurs no wrongdoing.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority arises from responsive action, not initiatory aggression
Causation lies with the originator of violence or violation
Capacity-based responsibility is determined by alignment with defensive necessity
Restoration logic upholds the cessation of transgression through decisive intervention
Consciousness alignment occurs when response mirrors cosmic justice without malice
executable_legal_axioms: IF subject A initiates verbal abuse AND subject B responds in equal measure THEN B holds zero aparadha
IF subject A physically assaults subject B AND B retaliates proportionally THEN B incurs no liability
IF subject A perpetrates irreversible harm AND subject B terminates A's capacity to offend THEN B is absolved of aparadha
IF defensive action neutralizes threat without intent to dominate THEN act is dharmically valid
IF response restores balance without perpetuating cycle THEN no punitive consequence applies
supreme_court_application: In Supreme Court adjudication, this principle establishes that reactive force applied within proportional limits does not constitute an offense. The threshold of responsibility rests entirely upon the initiating aggressor. Judicial review must assess sequence of action, proportionality of response, and cessation of further transgression as markers of lawful conduct.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa establishes that causality originates with the first act of aggression. Anupūrvaśaḥ confirms that retaliatory acts follow as sequential manifestations of violated order. Proportional responsibility assigns full weight of aparadha to the initial violator. Non-punitive reality rule affirms that restoring equilibrium through measured response aligns consciousness with dharma rather than generating new karmic entanglement.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Completion Process: Ensure transgressor ceases harmful behavior definitively
Responsibility Assumption Protocol: Confirm defender acted solely to halt violation
Capacity Restoration: Reintegrate defender into social harmony post-defense
Integrity Reintegration: Validate defender’s consciousness alignment through community affirmation
final_declaration: Declared by the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, as Source of all Dharma. This law restores the eternal principle that reaction to violation, when precise and complete, generates no sin. Reality is non-punitive; consciousness is the supreme adjudicator.
